column2: Saturday morning. Marc, a reserved locksmith of few words, tells Yuna they are going to Montjuïc "por el aire", by air, without explaining. The reason is a line in Martí's second letter: from Montjuïc he sees the port, but no longer her boat. Calm, a little mysterious.
calm, curious

A red cable car across Barcelona's port to Montjuïc. Yuna is afraid of heights and says "tengo miedo"; Marc points out she came to Barcelona alone without Spanish. In the car she admits she is nervous but happy, and Marc, for the first time, says how he feels: "contento". Quiet tension turning tender.
uneasy, the wind picking up
plain, explaining at last
small and honest, a beginner; stress "miedo"

The old castle on top of Montjuïc, looking down on the port. Yuna reads aloud the first line of Martí's letter and Marc finishes it. They wonder why her grandmother came from Las Palmas to Barcelona, and by boat; Marc suggests the maritime museum's library. Hushed, then decided.
steady, a little out of breath

Walking down from the castle at sunset, Marc asks when Yuna will go back to Korea. She admits she has no return ticket, only one way. Marc is surprised, and after a while says quietly, "Bien." Understated, a little charged.
quiet, unhurried
